chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-H ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When a man permits his slave to acquire concubines from his wealth, then he may buy as many as he desires, after he has been permitted to do so.

key_terms.عَبْدِهِ: his slave (male or female, contextually female concubine here)
key_terms.يَتَسَرَّى: to acquire concubines / to take concubines

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave buying concubines with his own money if the master permits it?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial autonomy of a slave (mudabbad) who has been granted permission to purchase female concubines using his own wealth. It establishes that the master's consent transforms the slave's personal funds into a valid medium for acquiring multiple concubines, reflecting the specific property rights and social structures of the early Islamic period. This ruling underscores the legal distinction between the slave's earnings and the master's direct ownership, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding manumission and property.
